intro: Follow the trail from Vimy to victory during an unforgettable day on the battlefields of the Artois! Explore the preserved trenches, tunnels, and battlefield of Vimy Ridge before visiting the iconic Canadian National Vimy Memorial, one of Canada's most important national monuments.

After lunch, continue to the battlefields of Hill 70, Monchy-le-Preux, and the Hundred Days Offensive where Canadian and Newfoundland soldiers achieved some of the most remarkable victories of the war. Along the way, visit both iconic, must-see landmarks and lesser-known battlefield locations that bring you into the footsteps of soldiers and reveal the full and heroic story of Canada's contribution in the First World War.

intro: Journey through the infamous Flanders Fields battlefields and discover what inspired the war's most poignant poem. During the Great War, this small corner of Belgium witnessed some of the fiercest fighting of the First World War. Stand where Canadian soldiers stood facing chlorine gas clouds and went over the top through the mud and devastation of Passchendaele.

From the Christmas Truce battlefield of 1914 to the ridges and cemeteries of Flanders, this tour explores both the famous and not-so-famous side of Flanders Fields. Walk preserved trenches, visit battlefield memorials, and gain a deeper understanding of the sacrifices made by Canadian soldiers in Belgium. The day concludes with attendance at the moving nightly Last Post Ceremony beneath the Menin Gate Memorial in Ypres, where more than 54,000 missing Canadian and Commonwealth soldiers are commemorated.

intro: Explore the preserved battlefield of the Beaumont-Hamel Newfoundland Memorial, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and walk through original trenches and No Man's Land. Later, as we venture off the beaten path, we see what is left of Canada's bloodiest battlefield of Courcelette, where more than 24,000 Canadians were killed or wounded in 1916.

In the afternoon, visit the Amiens battlefield where the Canadian Corps spearheaded the offensive that would become the blackest day for the German army, marking the beginning of the end of the First World War.

intro: Journey across two world wars during an unforgettable five-day battlefield tour through France and Belgium.

Beginning in the historic city of Arras, the first two days follow the Canadians across the Western Front. Explore the preserved trenches and tunnels of Vimy Ridge, visit the battlefields of Hill 70 and Canada's Hundred Days, and travel into Belgium to walk the ground at Ypres and Passchendaele. The Western Front portion concludes beneath the Menin Gate with the moving nightly Last Post Ceremony.

The journey then continues through Normandy to Bayeux. Cross Pegasus Bridge, follow the American airborne divisions through the fields and villages behind Utah Beach, and explore Pointe du Hoc, Omaha Beach and the Normandy American Cemetery.

Combining Canada's most important First World War battlefields with the celebrated D-Day sites of Normandy, this tour is ideal for travellers seeking a comprehensive introduction to the two defining conflicts of the twentieth century.

intro: Leave Paris behind for an unforgettable journey to the Normandy coast and discover the remarkable story of the brave Canadians who landed at Juno Beach in 1944.

Walk the sands where Canadian soldiers stormed ashore under devastating fire. See the famous Canada House at Bernières-sur-Mer and explore the surviving German defences of Hitler's Atlantic Wall. At the Juno Beach Centre, discover Canada's story and follow an expert Canadian guide into original German bunkers overlooking the landing beach.

After lunch in the seaside town of Courseulles-sur-Mer, continue inland along the route followed by Canadian soldiers on D-Day. Pay your respects at Bény-sur-Mer Canadian War Cemetery, stand at Hell's Corner near the furthest point reached by Canadian troops on June 6, and visit the historic Abbaye d'Ardenne.

intro: Stand on Juno Beach, where brave Canadians famously broke Hitler's Atlantic Wall under intense fire on D-Day. Explore the surviving German coastal defences and visit the Juno Beach Centre, Canada's main memorial and museum in Normandy.

Your journey continues beyond the beaches, tracing the Canadian advance through the villages and fields outside the historic city of Caen. Visit the battlefield of Authie, the Waffen SS headquarters at Abbaye d'Ardenne, Carpiquet and Hill 67, where Canadian soldiers faced some of the most determined German resistance of the Normandy campaign.
Along the way, visit both iconic landmarks and lesser-known battlefield locations that reveal the courage, sacrifice and achievements of the Canadians who liberated France in the summer of 1944.

intro: Discover the full story of the Allied landings in Normandy during an immersive two-day battlefield tour based in the historic town of Bayeux.

From the American airborne battlefields and the sands of Omaha Beach to the British and Canadian landing sectors at Gold and Juno, this tour follows the events of June 6, 1944, across the breadth of the Normandy invasion area.

Walk through preserved German gun positions, stand on the beaches where Allied soldiers came ashore and follow the footsteps of the paratroopers who landed behind enemy lines during the opening hours of D-Day.

itinerary.note: The first day begins with the American airborne landings west of Sainte-Mère-Église, where paratroopers of the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions descended into the fields and villages of Normandy during the early hours of June 6, 1944. Walk in the footsteps of Easy Company and learn about the assault on the German artillery positions at Brécourt Manor before the dramatic battlefield at Pointe du Hoc and the Normandy American Cemetery.

Follow the American paratroopers through the fields around Sainte-Mère-Église, stand on the sands of Omaha, explore the British and Canadian landing sectors and visit the site of the daring assault on Pegasus Bridge.

Beyond the battlefields, travel through the picturesque villages of the Pays d'Auge, sample the flavours of Normandy along the Route du Cidre and discover the historic towns of Lisieux, Cabourg and Bayeux.

name: The Dieppe Raid
enquiryNote: Send us a message with your preferred date and the number of guests, and we'll confirm availability directly.
scheduleFull: Departs Dieppe Monday to Friday, subject to availability. Private and customized versions of this tour are also available upon request.

cardAlt: The shingle beach, seafront lawns and town of Dieppe seen from the clifftop above the promenade
cardDesc: Blue Beach at Puys, the Pourville battlefield, surviving Atlantic Wall defences, and Dieppe Canadian War Cemetery.
intro: On 19 August 1942, more than 6,000 Allied troops, most of them Canadian, landed along the coast of occupied France during the Dieppe Raid. Within hours, the operation had ended in disaster, leaving thousands killed, wounded or captured.

Beginning in Dieppe, this full-day battlefield tour follows the Canadians from the beaches where they came ashore to the surrounding cliffs, villages and fortified positions that shaped the battle. Stand on Blue Beach at Puys, explore the battlefield at Pourville and discover surviving Atlantic Wall defences hidden among the picturesque white cliffs of the Normandy coast.
The day concludes at Dieppe Canadian War Cemetery, where many of those who fell during the raid remain buried.

Although historians continue to debate its legacy, the Dieppe Raid exposed serious weaknesses in Allied amphibious planning. Many of its lessons influenced preparations for the Normandy landings and the successful Canadian assault on Juno Beach less than two years later.
